title: SQL Set 05: Healthcare Appointments, Streaks & Coalescing
description: Date gaps/consecutive visits via LEAD, doctor billing totals, first-visit attribution, and multi-condition filtering.

queries.title: Earliest Appointment Date & Doctor per Patient
queries.prompt: For each patient in `appointments`, return `patient_id`, `visit_date`, and `doctor_name` corresponding to their chronologically earliest appointment. Order by `patient_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE appointments (appt_id INT PRIMARY KEY, patient_id INT, visit_date TEXT, doctor_name TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: WITH ordered AS (SELECT patient_id, visit_date, doctor_name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY visit_date ASC, appt_id ASC) AS rn FROM appointments) SELECT patient_id, visit_date, doctor_name FROM ordered WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY patient_id;
queries.explanation: Partitioning by `patient_id` ordered by `visit_date ASC` cleanly retrieves the first visit without correlated subqueries.

queries.title: Patients Readmitted Within 7 Days
queries.prompt: Find distinct `patient_id` values who had two consecutive visits in `ward_logs` where the next `admit_date` is within 7 days (1 to 7 days inclusive) after the previous `admit_date`. Order by `patient_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE ward_logs (log_id INT PRIMARY KEY, patient_id INT, admit_date TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: WITH diff AS (SELECT patient_id, julianday(admit_date) - julianday(LAG(admit_date) OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY admit_date)) AS gap FROM ward_logs) SELECT DISTINCT patient_id FROM diff WHERE gap BETWEEN 1 AND 7 ORDER BY patient_id;
queries.explanation: `julianday()` computes exact day differences in SQLite between consecutive admissions ordered via `LAG()`.

queries.title: Net Patient Payable After Insurance Coverage
queries.prompt: Compute `bill_id`, `patient_name`, and `net_payable` (`total_charge - COALESCE(insurance_covered, 0)`), filtering only rows where `net_payable >= 1000`. Order by `bill_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE billing (bill_id INT PRIMARY KEY, patient_name TEXT, total_charge INT, insurance_covered INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT bill_id, patient_name, total_charge - COALESCE(insurance_covered, 0) AS net_payable FROM billing WHERE total_charge - COALESCE(insurance_covered, 0) >= 1000 ORDER BY bill_id;
queries.explanation: Without `COALESCE`, `1800 - NULL` evaluates to `NULL` and Geeta would be silently dropped.

queries.title: Specialties Exceeding Hospital Average Fee
queries.prompt: Return `specialty` and `avg_fee` (rounded to 2 decimals) for medical specialties whose average consultation fee exceeds the overall average fee of all doctors. Order by `avg_fee` descending.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE doctors (doc_id INT PRIMARY KEY, specialty TEXT, fee INT);
queries.solutionSql: SELECT specialty, ROUND(AVG(fee), 2) AS avg_fee FROM doctors GROUP BY specialty HAVING AVG(fee) > (SELECT AVG(fee) FROM doctors) ORDER BY avg_fee DESC;
queries.explanation: Overall average fee is 900; `HAVING AVG(fee) > (SELECT AVG(fee) FROM doctors)` filters groups against the global scalar subquery.

queries.title: Keep Latest Record per Phone Number
queries.prompt: From `patient_contacts` containing duplicate `phone` registrations, return the single most recent row (`contact_id`, `phone`, `updated_at`) per `phone` based on largest `updated_at` (tie-break largest `contact_id`). Order by `contact_id`.
queries.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE patient_contacts (contact_id INT PRIMARY KEY, phone TEXT, updated_at TEXT);
queries.solutionSql: WITH cte AS (SELECT contact_id, phone, updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY phone ORDER BY updated_at DESC, contact_id DESC) AS rn FROM patient_contacts) SELECT contact_id, phone, updated_at FROM cte WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY contact_id;
queries.explanation: Common SQL deduplication pattern using `ROW_NUMBER()` over `phone` ordered by recency descending.
